newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodia condemns attack, journalists in fear.
newsitem.headline: Cambodia condemns attack, journalists in fear.

text.p: Cambodian leaders on Tuesday condemned a deadly grenade attack on a local television station, but journalists feared the media remained an easy target for settling political scores.
"The media is now a weapon...in political conflicts. It is a really difficult situation," Khmer Journalists Association President Pin Samkhon told Reuters.

He said the independent press was under strong pressure from political tensions in Cambodia, where co-Premiers Prince Norodom Ranariddh and Hun Sen have clashed over power-sharing issues, recent political violence and the role of the monarchy.
On Sunday, seven unidentified gunmen killed an announcer and wounded two other people in a grenade attack on a state-run television station in the southern port city of Sihanoukville.
The gunmen opened fire with AK-47 assault rifles and rocket-propelled grenades, destroying broadcasting equipment in an attack officials said they suspected was political.
They said the station had declined to air a statement by an official from Ranariddh's FUNCINPEC party attacking Hun Sen's Cambodian People's Party.
Local police on Tuesday said they had no leads and noted tensions were high in the provincial city.
In a statement from his cabinet, Ranariddh said the attack "seriously affected the freedom of the press" and ordered an immediate investigation.
Secretary of State for Information Khieu Kanharith, a member of Hun Sen's party, also condemned the attack.
But despite the dismay over the attack, Cambodian journalists said they feared the incident could be the first of many as national elections approach next year.
Hun Sen and Ranariddh are expected to oppose each other in the polls.

Their political differences are often reflected in the print and broadcast media, which usually have clear political allegiances. Newspapers typically run bitter attacks that characterise politicians as barnyard animals or accuse them of involvement in criminal activities without substantiation.
Pin Samkhon said that with current political pressures, few journalists could resist pressure to speak on behalf of a party.
More than ten violent incidents have been reported against journalists in the past three years, resulting in four deaths.
